To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) the prevalence of breast cancer is higher in elderly women than in younger women and (b) the prognosis of elderly women is poorer than younger women.

(i) breast cancer is a common disease in elderly patients, and the incidence is increasing; (ii) breast cancer in older patients is associated with favourable tumour biology; (iii) elderly patients are more likely to have advanced tumours and are less likely to adhere to standard treatment protocols; (iv) age alone should not be a criterion for withholding treatment; (v) the presence of comorbidities or poor functional status is a significant prognostic factor; and (vi)

(1) age alone should not be a criterion for treatment; (2) elderly patients are less likely than younger patients to be treated according the guidelines and this is associated with poorer survival; (3) comorbidities, functional status, nutritional status and geriatric syndromes are all important prognostic factors and should be assessed in all elderly patients; and (4) the multidisciplinary approach is of paramount importance in the management of elderly patients.
